text: Using a two-phase curriculum that begins with confident weak-labeled examples and then expands to the full weak-labeled set, with the second phase run at a learning-rate scale of 0.1, we measure a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.82 on the ANLI testbed. This figure is averaged over num_seeds = 4 seeds, which is a small sample, and no per-seed spread or standard error was recorded, so the run-to-run variability of this number is unknown from the data at hand. Importantly, no baseline PGR was supplied for comparison, so this result cannot be characterized as an improvement over single-phase training on the full weak-labeled data or over any other reference method; it stands only as a standalone measurement of the curriculum configuration described. Establishing whether the two-phase schedule and the reduced phase-two learning rate contribute anything would require a matched baseline, additional seeds, and reported variance.
